text: What did I do today that I would do again on my best day?
evaluation: Solo question. The point is to notice. Be specific.

text: What did I do today that I would not do on my best day?
evaluation: No flagellation. Just naming. The next answer is the work.

text: What was the smallest moment of beauty I noticed today?
evaluation: Notice the noticing. If nothing comes, that itself is information.

text: What was the smallest moment of cruelty I let pass today?
evaluation: Cruelty includes my own. Letting it pass is a moral act.

text: What am I avoiding right now, in this room?
evaluation: Bodily question. Often the avoidance is in plain view.

text: What am I avoiding right now, that lives outside this room?
evaluation: Bigger frame. Whatever surfaces is the next agenda item.

text: What do I want today that I do not want this year?
evaluation: Catches impulse-want versus considered-want. Hold the difference.

text: What do I want this year that I do not want today?
evaluation: Counterpart. Trains the muscle of long-want.

text: What do I find easy that I have stopped giving myself credit for?
evaluation: Strengths normalised by repetition. Re-see them.

text: What do I find hard that I have been pretending is easy?
evaluation: The pretence costs more than the difficulty.

text: What do I do that I think is generous and might be control?
evaluation: A hard mirror. The reflex to defend is the answer.

text: What do I do that I think is restraint and might be cowardice?
evaluation: Same shape. Sit with it.

text: What is one belief I hold that I would defend less if pressed?
evaluation: Beliefs that survive pressure are different from beliefs we inherit.

text: What is one belief I hold that I would defend more, if I were honest?
evaluation: We often soften our convictions to fit our company. Restore them in private.

text: What am I building, in my life, without realising I'm building it?
evaluation: Habits are buildings. Look up.

text: What am I tearing down, in my life, without realising I'm tearing it down?
evaluation: Same. The damage is rarely intentional, which is exactly what makes it hard to see.

text: Whose voice do I still hear when I judge myself, and is it accurate?
evaluation: Naming the voice loosens it.

text: Whose voice do I want in my head, that I have not let in?
evaluation: Counterpart. Choose the witness on purpose.

text: What part of my body am I at war with, and what would peace look like?
evaluation: The 'peace look like' clause is the work. Don't skip it.

text: What part of my body have I made peace with, and how?
evaluation: Hard-won. Worth recalling on bad days.

text: What in my life have I outgrown but not put down?
evaluation: Habits, identities, relationships. Specificity matters.

text: What in my life is still ahead of me, that I have not started?
evaluation: Honest aspiration without 'someday' protection.

text: What did I want at twenty that I am glad I didn't get?
evaluation: Reframes failure into curation.

text: What did I want at twenty that I still want, only quieter?
evaluation: Continuity is information.

text: What lie have I told myself this week?
evaluation: Be specific. Vague self-criticism is its own evasion.

text: What truth have I told myself this week that I almost didn't?
evaluation: Credit yourself for the near-miss.

text: What in my routine is autopilot, and is autopilot serving me?
evaluation: Autopilot is sometimes peace and sometimes drift. Distinguish.

text: What in my routine is performance, and for whom?
evaluation: Performance for an absent audience is the most expensive kind.

text: What kind of stranger do I want to be?
evaluation: How we treat people we will never see again is who we are.

text: What kind of stranger have I been, lately?
evaluation: Hold the gap between si029 and si030 without flinching.

text: What is one thing I do every day that I love?
evaluation: Don't reach for the impressive. The mundane true thing wins.

text: What is one thing I do every day that I dislike, and could change?
evaluation: If 'could' becomes 'will', name the date.

text: What am I waiting for permission to do, and from whom?
evaluation: The permission-giver is often imaginary. Name them anyway.

text: What have I given myself permission for, recently, that surprised me?
evaluation: Credit. Repeat the move.

text: What is one thing I am proud of that no one knows about?
evaluation: Private pride is healthier than performed pride. Stay there.

text: What is one thing I am ashamed of that no one knows about?
evaluation: Naming, even silently in a notebook, lessens the weight by a measurable amount.

text: What is the smallest thing that consistently makes me feel okay?
evaluation: Build the day around it.

text: What is the smallest thing that consistently makes me feel worse?
evaluation: Subtract before you add.

text: What is one fear I have outgrown, and how did that happen?
evaluation: The 'how' part is the playbook for the next fear.

text: What is one fear I have grown into?
evaluation: Adult fears are stranger. Name them without dramatising.

text: What is one decision I have been delaying with research?
evaluation: Research is sometimes wisdom and sometimes hiding. Distinguish.

text: What is one decision I have made too quickly, and what was the cost?
evaluation: Both delay and haste are evasions of the actual choice.

text: What in my life is provisional that I have been treating as permanent?
evaluation: Misclassification of permanence is a quiet trap.

text: What in my life is permanent that I have been treating as provisional?
evaluation: The reverse. Equally costly.

text: What is one relationship in my life that needs more from me than I have been giving?
evaluation: Don't promise. Just notice. Then choose, separately.

text: What is one relationship in my life that has been getting more than its share?
evaluation: Counterpart. Both can be true.

text: What is one obligation I keep that I could ethically drop?
evaluation: Many obligations are inherited rather than chosen.

text: What is one obligation I have dropped that I should ethically pick back up?
evaluation: Pair with si047. Honesty cuts both ways.

text: What part of my work is craft, and what part is performance?
evaluation: Both have their place. Conflating them is the trap.

text: What part of my work am I doing because no one else will?
evaluation: Gratifying for a while; expensive over years. Audit.

text: What is one ambition I have that I would still hold if no one ever knew?
evaluation: Filters out status-want. The remainder is your real ambition.

text: What is one ambition I have that exists mostly because of others?
evaluation: Inherited ambitions are real but not necessarily yours.

text: What in my financial life is anxiety, and what in it is reality?
evaluation: Distinguish before deciding. Both can be present at once.

text: What is the most expensive thing I have bought that I do not regret?
evaluation: Calibrates what 'worth it' means for you, in your own terms.

text: What is the most expensive thing I have bought that I do regret?
evaluation: Money lessons are cheaper to learn from regret than from another purchase.

text: What is one habit I am developing without yet calling it a habit?
evaluation: Frequency turns into character. Watch the slope.

text: What is one habit I have lost that I miss?
evaluation: Recovery is often less work than expected.

text: What is one habit I have lost that I should let stay lost?
evaluation: Permission to not romanticise.

text: What is one assumption about my future that I should test?
evaluation: Tested assumptions are more useful than reassuring ones.

text: What is one assumption about my past that I should revisit?
evaluation: We rewrite the past selectively. Revisit one chapter on purpose.

text: What in my life right now would my fifteen-year-old self find astonishing, in either direction?
evaluation: Both directions are useful. Pride and shame are equally informative.

text: What in my life right now would my eighty-year-old self thank me for?
evaluation: Long-arc question. Don't aim for grandeur.

text: What in my life right now would my eighty-year-old self ask me to stop?
evaluation: Worth taking seriously even when uncomfortable.

text: What is one thing I have stopped doing for myself that I should restart, this week?
evaluation: Specific. This week, not someday.

text: What is one thing I have started doing for myself that I should keep?
evaluation: Credit before correction.

text: What is one thing I do for others that quietly drains me?
evaluation: Generosity that drains is unsustainable. The fix is rarely guilt; it's redesign.

text: What is one thing I do for others that fills me, and how often do I do it?
evaluation: Many of us under-do the things that fill us. Schedule one.

text: Where is my attention going that I have not chosen?
evaluation: Attention is the one truly finite asset. Audit it.

text: Where is my attention going that I would defend, even if criticised?
evaluation: Defensible attention is a small honest map of self.

text: What in my inner life have I been performing for an imagined audience?
evaluation: Even our private thoughts perform sometimes. Notice for whom.

text: What in my inner life is honestly mine, with no audience at all?
evaluation: Pair with si070. Build more in this corner.

text: What is one form of comfort I take that has begun to numb instead of soothe?
evaluation: Comforts decay. Notice the slide before it requires intervention.

text: What is one form of discomfort I avoid that I would benefit from accepting?
evaluation: Specific. Not 'all discomfort'. One thing.

text: What in my faith or unbelief has shifted, quietly, in the last year?
evaluation: Shifts are often invisible to the person shifting. Look on purpose.

text: What in my faith or unbelief have I stopped examining?
evaluation: What we stop examining ossifies. Choose what to keep examining.

text: What is the conversation I am most avoiding with myself?
evaluation: Don't have it tonight. Just name it. Tonight is enough.

text: What is the conversation I have already had with myself, that I haven't acted on?
evaluation: Knowing the answer is half. The other half is the harder half.

text: What is one place in my life where I am pretending the rules don't apply to me?
evaluation: Honest answer is rarely about laws. More often about decency, sleep, or attention.

text: What is one place in my life where I am applying rules that don't actually exist?
evaluation: Phantom rules cost more than real ones.

text: What is one moment of grace I have refused to receive?
evaluation: Receiving is harder than giving for many. Notice the refusal pattern.

text: What is one moment of grace I have given without knowing it landed?
evaluation: Quiet credit. Don't go looking for confirmation; just hold it.

text: What is one place in my life where I am still my parents' child?
evaluation: Inheritance, good and bad. Naming reduces unconscious transmission.

text: What is one place in my life where I am clearly not my parents' child?
evaluation: Differentiation deserves its credit.

text: What is one true sentence about yourself, today?
evaluation: Short. Hard. Don't decorate.

text: What is one true sentence about my life, today?
evaluation: Distinct from si084. The life and the self diverge sometimes.

text: What in me is closed that I want open, and what is open that I want closed?
evaluation: Both calibrations matter. We tend to focus on one direction.

text: What did I last give my best attention to, and how did it feel?
evaluation: Best attention is rarer than spending. Notice the feel of it.

text: What did I last withhold attention from that needed it, and what did I give it to instead?
evaluation: Substitution audit. Often phone or food. Be honest.

text: What is one truth I tell my friends that I should be telling myself?
evaluation: We're often gentler with friends than with the self. Borrow that voice.

text: What is one truth I tell myself that I should be telling my friends?
evaluation: The reverse. Both are common.

text: What is one fear I have, today, that has nothing to do with anything actually happening?
evaluation: Distinguish forecast from event. Often the forecast is the only suffering.

text: What is one fear I have, today, that I am ignoring because it has no easy solution?
evaluation: Acknowledgement is not the same as solution.

text: What does my body know about my life that my mind has not admitted?
evaluation: Locate it physically. Tightness, fatigue, ease. The body is rarely wrong about the basics.

text: What does my mind know about my life that my body has not caught up to?
evaluation: The reverse direction. Often: knowing one needs sleep, rest, less, more.

text: What is one thing I would do tomorrow if I were certain I would not be judged?
evaluation: Then ask whether the judgement is real, and whose, and what it would cost.

text: What is one thing I would not do tomorrow if I were certain no one would notice?
evaluation: Performance audit. Disconcerting. Useful.

text: What is the smallest, hardest, most useful thing I could do this week?
evaluation: All three adjectives are required. Not all big things, not all easy things.

text: What is one thing I would forgive myself for, if asked aloud, today?
evaluation: Self-forgiveness rarely arrives unprompted. Prompt it.

text: What is one thing I am quietly grateful for, that I haven't said?
evaluation: Say it. Even just to the page.

text: What is the next true thing?
evaluation: Closing. Whatever surfaces is the line of the session. Write it down.
